newsitem.title: FINLAND: Benefon sees H2 op profit down on H1.
newsitem.headline: Benefon sees H2 op profit down on H1.

text.p: Finnish mobile phone maker Benefon Oy said in a statement on Tuesday that its operating profit for the second half of 1996 would be somewhat lower than for the first half.
"The operating profit of the second half seems to become somewhat lower than the operating profit of the first half of the year," Benefon said.

In a statement, the company blamed its outlook for lower second half operating profit on slower net sales growth than expected when it issued interim results in August and on "quite high" spending on research and development and marketing in recent months.
"It is now obvious that the net sales for the second half will not grow very much from that of the first half of the year," it said.

In August, Benefon reported first half operating profit of 14.8 million markka, down from 29.8 million in the first half of 1995. Net sales in the first half amounted to 136.0 million markka, down from 141.6 million.
The company said the final type approval of its first GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) product had proceeded, but had not been achieved.

"Systematic honing of the user quality and the producibility of the product together with the field tests has continued during the approval process," it said and added that it would eventually report the type approval separately.
Benefon said the GSM mobile phone market had remained strong as a whole, as well as in countries where the company is active.
